column2: Definition of Rights: Reasonable claims of individuals recognized by society and sanctioned by law
Enforceability: Claims become rights only when written into law and enforceable by courts
Reciprocity: Every right carries a duty to respect the rights of others
Role in Democracy: Rights enable citizens to express views, form parties, and participate in politics
Protection against Majority: Rights protect minorities from oppression by the majority
Guantanamo Bay Case: Prisoners were detained without trial, violating international human rights laws
Saudi Arabia Case: Absolute monarchy with no political parties, religious freedom, or equal rights for women
Kosovo Case: Elected government carried out ethnic massacre against a minority community
Basic Feature of Constitution: Fundamental Rights are essential for life and democracy

column3: Rule of Law: Law applies equally to all citizens without exception
Non-Discrimination: State cannot discriminate on religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth
Equality of Opportunity: Equal access to public employment with reservations for disadvantaged groups
Abolition of Untouchability: Practice is banned and punishable by law
Six Basic Freedoms: Speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession
Personal Liberty: Life and liberty can be taken only by legal procedure
Arrest Safeguards: Arrested persons must be informed, produced before magistrate, and allowed a lawyer
Prohibition of Trafficking: Buying and selling of human beings is banned
Ban on Forced Labour: Begar and bonded labour are prohibited
Child Labour Prohibition: Children below 14 cannot work in hazardous industries
Secularism: State has no official religion and treats all religions equally
Religious Freedom: Citizens may profess, practice, and propagate religion peacefully
State Neutrality: Government cannot promote or fund any religion
Minority Protection: Minorities can preserve their language and culture
Educational Institutions: Minorities can establish and manage educational institutions
Enforcement of Rights: Citizens can directly approach courts for protection of rights
Heart and Soul of Constitution: Described so by Dr. Ambedkar

column2: Public Interest Litigation: Any citizen can seek justice for public interest
National Human Rights Commission: Independent body protecting human rights since 1993
New Derived Rights: Includes Right to Information and Right to Education
Expanded Right to Life: Supreme Court includes Right to Food under Right to Life
